title: Dynlink: loading plug-ins at run time
body: A program normally contains every module it will ever run. The `dynlink` library lets a native program load compiled code *while it is running*: `Dynlink.loadfile "plugin.cmxs"` links a shared object (`.cmxs`) built with `ocamlopt -shared`, runs its top-level code, and adds its modules to the program. The host and the plug-in must agree on the interfaces they share, which the loader checks with module checksums.

The usual design is a small *registry* library that both sides link. The host loads whatever plug-in the user names; each plug-in's top-level code calls `Registry.register name f`, and the host then finds the new entries in the registry. Because the plug-in only depends on the registry's interface, new behaviour is added without recompiling or even restarting the host. Dune builds the shared object for a library with the target `plugins/double.cmxs`.

Loading code is a trust decision: a plug-in runs with the full privileges of the host, so load only code you control. Handle `Dynlink.Error` and report it, since a missing file, a wrong compiler version or an interface mismatch are all normal failure modes.
challenge: plugins/double.ml registers a function named "double" that returns its argument unchanged. Fix it so the plug-in doubles its input, so that running the host on the built plug-in prints `double: 42` for the input 21.
projectInstructions: Build with `dune build --root . plugins/double.cmxs host/host.exe`, then run `_build/default/host/host.exe _build/default/plugins/double.cmxs`. Edit only plugins/double.ml, then rebuild and run again.
question: Why do the host and the plug-in both link the small registry library?
correct: It is the interface they share: the plug-in registers into it and the host reads from it, with no recompilation of the host
wrong: Dynlink cannot load a plug-in that has no dependencies
The registry is the only module the compiler is able to link
reasoning: A fixed shared interface lets independently built code cooperate at run time while the loader verifies the interfaces still match.
